A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GraphNC research. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and complete Appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including material moved between the appendices and main text.

before.justification: v2 reports original six-dataset experiments, teacher-model comparisons, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds RHO comparisons, additional ablations, a two-stage training control, and threshold and augmentation analyses.

M1.justification: New Appendix C.8 introduces the evaluated GraphNC-RED variant, replacing feature masking with random edge dropping. This is a limited procedural adaptation; the default GraphNC architecture, ScoreDA and NormReg objectives, inference procedure, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Amazon, T-Finance, Reddit, YelpChi, Tolokers, and Photo for the same node-anomaly detection task. The degraded-teacher scenario already appears in v2. The new controls and augmentation experiments retain this data and task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds RHO to Table 1 and the two-stage GGAD** comparator in Figure 8, retaining the previous baselines. Ablation comparisons also gain GraphNC-RED and all-node NormReg variants for DOMINANT and OCGNN.

E3.justification: The main 15% labeled-normal training setting and AUROC/AUPRC metrics remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce GGAD** training with a 0.7 pseudo-label threshold and BCE, FP/FN evaluation at thresholds 0.7, 0.8, and 0.9, and alternative augmentation and regularization controls.

E4.justification: Appendices C.6–C.8 substantially extend diagnostic validation by testing whether gains arise merely from two-stage training, depend on decision thresholds, or require feature masking rather than edge dropping. The existing other-teacher ablation moves from v2 Appendix C.3/Table 6 to v3 Section 5.4/Table 4 and gains all-node NormReg results.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five independent runs with different random seeds. v3 introduces no changed run-count disclosure, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Substantial result sets are added for RHO, GGAD**, GraphNC-RED, expanded ablations, and threshold-specific errors; matched original scores remain unchanged. RHO becomes the strongest average comparator and changes dataset-level rankings: on T-Finance its AUROC/AUPRC are 0.8623/0.4893 versus GraphNC's retained 0.8340/0.3667. GraphNC retains the best Table 1 averages.

T1.justification: The method equations, Theorems 4.1 and D.1, Appendix D assumptions and proof, and Appendix E complexity analysis retain the same mathematical content. Changes are punctuation and placement.

C1.justification: The core claims remain normality calibration through ScoreDA and NormReg, improvement across three teacher families and six benchmarks, and state-of-the-art performance. The stronger-teacher statement disappears from one contribution bullet but remains in the introduction and Section 5.2.

C2.justification: New discussion attributes GGAD**'s T-Finance advantage to threshold choice and cautions about unstable pseudo-label supervision. Appendix C.8 explains masking and edge dropping through regularization and invariant representations, while qualifying their benefits as dataset dependent. The original teacher-dependence limitation remains.

D1.justification: The abstract changes code access from a promised release to reported availability at the same repository. Appendix C.6 documents the GGAD** construction, pseudo-label threshold, and BCE training. Existing software, hardware, and default GraphNC hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Ai et al.'s RHO work and Yan et al. (2025), with substantive RHO positioning in Section 2 and its description in Appendix B. InterLUDE and the video-anomaly survey receive publication-information updates rather than becoming newly cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected paragraphs are edited, other-teacher ablations receive a main-text subsection, and appendix headings are reorganized around the added analyses. Affiliations, proceedings text, and acknowledgments are updated. Most exposition and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 corrects FPR/FNR labels to FP/FN while retaining the plotted counts. Table 1 gains RHO rows; the other-teacher ablation table is relocated and expanded. Figures 8–9 and Table 9 are new, while existing plots are retained, including the runtime figure renumbered from 8 to 10.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical scrutiny through the RHO comparison and new controls for two-stage training, thresholds, and augmentation, addressing gaps in v2's validation. Corrected FP/FN labels also improve clarity. These are useful gains, although Section 5.1 still overstates consistent superiority over RHO despite contrary dataset-level results in Table 1.
